newsitem.title: FRANCE: More rain freshens grain crops in France.
newsitem.headline: More rain freshens grain crops in France.

text.p: Grain areas in northern France soaked up more beneficial rain on Friday and showery weather was predicted through the weekend, weather office Meteo France said.

Arable areas north of the river Loire would get the most frequent bursts of rain on Friday afternoon. The weather across most of France remained blustery with intermittent breaks in the clouds, it said.
Fine weather was set to return on Monday after more scattered showers and heavy cloud cover over the weekend.

Steady rain for most of the week has improved the appearance of grain which had yellowed after four months of near drought and allowed maize farmers in the southwest to get on with sowings which had been delayed by dry, unmanageable soil.
But even as grain farmers celebrated, another group of farmers complained about the wet weather.
Fruit and vegetable lobby Interfel said rain and low temperatures had affected strawberry consumption while supplies of the fruit had soared because of import competition from Spain and Italy.

Strawberry growers demonstrated against cheap prices on Thursday by selling fruit at $2 a tray beneath the Eiffel Tower. The farmers, who enter the peak of their annual growing season next week, say they are being driven out of business by imports and cheap prices forced on them by supermarkets.
